clinician.trajectory_summary: A 48-year-old male with a history of polysubstance use (cocaine and methamphetamines) and positive COVID-19 PCR presented with 3 days of progressive, generalized, throbbing abdominal pain and nausea. Initial laboratory workup revealed normocytic anemia (hemoglobin 8.5 g/dL), acute kidney injury (creatinine 2.3 mg/dL), elevated venous lactate (6.3 with normal anion gap), and mildly elevated inflammatory markers (ESR 24 mm/hour, CRP 5.9 mg/dL, procalcitonin 1.31 ng/mL). CT imaging of the abdomen demonstrated a 2 cm lobulated saccular aneurysm involving the left gastric or splenic artery with moderate hemoperitoneum and hematomas (largest 8.6 cm) consistent with aneurysmal rupture. Additional imaging revealed fusiform dilation of the superior mesenteric artery. Celiac and splenic arteriograms confirmed a mid-splenic artery pseudoaneurysm, which was treated with IR-guided splenic artery embolization with coils, resulting in hemodynamic stability and no further bleeding. Hepatitis B and C serology were negative. The multi-vessel involvement with characteristic aneurysmal findings was consistent with polyarteritis nodosa. The patient was treated with high-dose IV methylprednisolone followed by IV cyclophosphamide (15 mg/kg every 2 weeks for 3 doses, then every 3 weeks for 3-6 months) with glucocorticoid taper. The diagnosis of PAN was made despite the patient not fulfilling the complete American College of Rheumatology (ACR) classification criteria for PAN.
